title: Changing a car tyre safely at the roadside
version: AA New Zealand 'How to change a car tyre' and 'Breakdown safety guide' pages; NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi Road Code pages 'If your vehicle breaks down' and 'Tips for handling driving emergencies' (tyre blowouts, read via NZTA's nzta2.cwp.govt.nz mirror); NZTA Drive pages 'Changing a tyre' and 'Dealing with a breakdown' (drive.govt.nz restricted-licence bonus skills); all read 20 Nov 2026 NZ time, no last-updated or review date shown on any page
sourceNote: The sites block direct download here (curl refused by the proxy for nzta.govt.nz, drive.govt.nz and aa.co.nz; web search gave titles only, no excerpts), so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote short exact sentences (long ones in pieces, rejoined); about 35 key lines (80km/h, 111, ***555, 'do not', 'never', 'don't', jacking and gear lines) were confirmed EXACT in a second read, but small slips (apostrophe style, joining punctuation marked [-]) are possible. Six labelled sections: A Road Code breakdowns (ordinary road and motorway), B Road Code tyre blowouts plus the hazard-light lines from other emergencies, C Drive changing a tyre (steps, nut-tightening order, jack safety, space saver, blowout pull-over steps), D Drive dealing with a breakdown, E AA how to change a tyre (main how-to: preparation, 13 steps, tricky models, heavy wheel), F AA breakdown safety guide (10 steps, 111 / ***555 / ***222). Left out: navigation, videos, link labels, 'next skill' links. Not captured: the rest of the Road Code emergencies page (only its blowout part and hazard-light lines), the AA 'Glovebox safety guide' PDF and the AA motoring-blog motorway article, any vehicle owner's manual. Oddities, gaps and contradictions: (1) no source gives a distance for a safety/warning triangle or says where to put it; only the Road Code mentions one at all, as an alternative ('hazard lights or use a safety triangle'), and no source says whether to carry one; (2) the AA breakdown guide says 'do not attempt to fix the vehicle yourself' while the AA tyre page and Drive teach changing the tyre yourself, and the AA tyre page mentions 'the side of the motorway' as a place it may happen; no source says whether it is safe to change a tyre on a motorway shoulder or what to do on a road or motorway with no shoulder; (3) nothing on which side of the car you may work on (traffic side) or standing clear of traffic while working, beyond 'don't stand in the road' / 'on the motorway' and AA 'Never attempt ... if your personal safety is at risk'; (4) no wheel-nut tightening value (torque) or advice to recheck nuts later: AA says 'tighten snugly' and you 'can stand on the wrench handle', Drive gives a top-opposite-left-right order and a shake test; AA gives no order; (5) space saver: both say not over 80km/h; AA adds not 'long distances' (no distance given), Drive says replace 'as soon as you can'; neither gives a tyre pressure; (6) gear when parked differs: AA 'in gear (if manual)', Drive first gear on the flat or uphill, reverse downhill; (7) blocking wheels: AA 'Block the wheels on the side not being lifted' with nothing on what to block with; Drive does not mention blocking; (8) passengers: AA and Drive say get everyone out of the car before jacking, but the AA breakdown guide says if it is safer to stay in, occupants sit away from traffic with seatbelts on, and Road Code/Drive say wait in the car; none says where passengers should wait while a tyre is changed; (9) lights differ: Road Code and Drive say the inside light at night, AA breakdown guide says parking lights when dark, raining or foggy; Road Code alone says hang something white on the door on a motorway; (10) emergency numbers: Drive gives *555, AA gives ***555 and ***222 (as written) and 111 for immediate risk; the AA tyre page gives 0800 500 222 for Roadservice; (11) blowout advice differs slightly: Road Code 'ease off the accelerator', Drive 'Brake slowly and smoothly' and 'Don't overcorrect'; (12) neither how-to says what to do if a wheel nut will not come off, the jack sinks or the spare is also flat, beyond AA calling Roadservice; (13) no advice on reflective or bright clothing, or night-time work beyond carrying a torch.
status: Reviewer: 5 instructions missed (incl. wheels straight and the emergency roadside phone) and 14 findings, all fixed. 118 of 118 quotes exact (web copy).
